newsitem.title: FRANCE: George 'perplexed' by stronger dollar calls - paper.
newsitem.headline: George 'perplexed' by stronger dollar calls - paper.

text.p: Bank of England governor Eddie George said in an interview published on Tuesday he was "perplexed" by calls for a stronger dollar to boost growth in Europe.
"This quest, which is essentially a French one, leaves me perplexed," George told Le Figaro daily.
"Those who express it are also those who call for a drop in German interest rates. I don't think that these are appropriate remedies for Europe in an overall sense," he said.
The dollar has risen three to four percent against leading European currencies since early November, but French authorities are believed to want more.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe said last month the U.S. currency was "chronically" undervalued, giving U.S. firms an unfair advantage.
Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said last week that the market may underestimate the underlying fundamentals of the dollar.
